title: Interlayer Fermi Polarons in Bilayer MoTe$_2$
authors: Ruihao Ni, Eugen Dizer, Maximilian Wolf, Son T. Le, Sharadh Jois, Jeffrey J. Schwartz, Liuxin Gu, Rundong Ma, Suji Park, Beini Gao, Lifu Zhang, Houk Jang, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Aubrey T. Hanbicki, Adam L. Friedman, Richard Schmidt, You Zhou
abstract: Atomic bilayers of transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) host quantum phases governed by the layer degree of freedom, including bilayer Wigner crystals, fractional Chern insulators, and exciton condensates. These phases are probed primarily through exciton spectroscopy, yet it remains poorly understood how excitons and carriers interact to form Fermi polarons in bilayers, where both the impurity and the Fermi sea carry a layer pseudospin. Progress has been limited because most TMD bilayers have momentum-indirect optical bandgaps, in which non-radiative decay and inhomogeneous broadening obscure the intrinsic spectra. Here, we show that bilayer MoTe$_2$, unlike most TMD bilayers, retains a direct optical bandgap, providing a clean platform for studying bilayer Fermi-polaron physics. In a dual-gated device, an out-of-plane electric field continuously tunes the hybridization between intralayer and interlayer excitons, forming layer-coherent excitons. Upon electrostatic doping, the excitonic spectrum evolves into multiple polaron branches, controlled by both carrier doping and the out-of-plane electric field. Among these, we identify a polaron with no analog in monolayers, in which a layer-coherent exciton is dressed by carriers in the opposite layer, and is quantitatively captured by our field-theoretic model. Our results establish that pseudospin structure in both the impurity and the bath reshapes polaron formation, opening new avenues to many-body states such as Bose-Einstein condensates with interlayer coherence.
summary: This work reports on the study of Fermi polarons in bilayer MoTe2, a TMD that provides a clean platform for such research. By tuning the electric field and doping, the researchers observe multiple polaron branches whose formation is governed by the layer pseudospin. This establishes a theoretical and experimental framework for understanding complex many-body states in vdW heterostructures.
main_problem: The paper investigates the formation and properties of Fermi polarons in bilayer Transition Metal Dichalcogenides (TMDs), focusing on how the layer pseudospin influences these many-body states.
main_result: They demonstrate that bilayer MoTe2 retains a direct optical bandgap, allowing the observation of multiple, tunable polaron branches whose structure is dictated by the interplay between carrier doping and an out-of-plane electric field.
method: The study combines experimental exciton spectroscopy (PL and reflectance) with a quantitative field-theoretic model based on the T-matrix approach.
model_or_system: The system is bilayer MoTe2, a TMD, studied in a dual-gated device. The physics involves excitons interacting with a free carrier Fermi sea, where both components carry a layer pseudospin.
key_observables: Multiple polaron branches ($	ext{AP}^{\pm}$, $	ext{RP}^{\pm}$, $	ext{IP}^+$), redshift/blueshift of spectral features, and the evolution of the excitonic spectrum with doping.
important_parameters: Out-of-plane electric field ($V_{	ext{BG}}$), electrostatic doping (carrier density), and the layer pseudospin structure.
main_assumptions: The theoretical modeling relies on a T-matrix approach and assumes a simplified electrostatic model for calculating electric fields and doping densities.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the device schematic, field-dependent reflectance maps showing interlayer excitons ($	ext{IX1}$, $	ext{IX2}$), and energy-derivative spectra showing the evolution of polaron branches across different doping regimes.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes MoTe2 as a clean platform due to its direct bandgap. It then systematically explores the doping- and electric-field-dependent evolution of the excitonic spectrum into distinct polaron branches, supported by both experimental measurements and theoretical fitting.
why_interesting: The explicit modeling of pseudospin structure in both the impurity and the bath to reshape polaron formation is highly relevant to understanding correlated phases in low-dimensional quantum materials, bridging concepts from quantum optics and condensed matter theory.
